disease_label_per_paper: Infective endocarditis caused by Streptococcus pluranimalium
presentation_summary: Three weeks of fever up to 39 C without respiratory, urinary, abdominal, skin, joint, or neurologic symptoms
Vital signs: BP 107/72 mmHg, SpO2 98% room air, HR 95/min, RR 20/min, temperature 39 C
Exam was unremarkable except for a harsh pansystolic murmur
Two sets of blood cultures grew Streptococcus pluranimalium, sensitive to vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid
TEE showed VSD and a small mobile mass attached to the septal wall on the right ventricular side, likely vegetation

risk_context.source_text_value: membranous ventricular septal defect of moderate size

observations.source_text_value: fever started three weeks before visiting the hospital as it reached 39 C; temperature 39 C
two sets of blood cultures were obtained and showed gram-positive cocci; two sets showed S. pluranimalium
Two sets of blood cultures showed S. pluranimalium
sensitive to vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid

actual_treatment: de-escalated to ceftriaxone for a total of four weeks
